options.reason: Absolute annual counts show the direct difference in recorded motorist and cyclist fatalities year by year.
options.answer: Motorist deaths exceeded cyclist deaths in every year; 2025 had 81 motorist deaths and 23 cyclist deaths, while annual peaks were 139 motorist deaths in 2020 and 31 cyclist deaths in 2019 and 2023.
options.interpretation: This framing answers the question in absolute annual counts: the paired bars show more motorist than cyclist deaths in every year, with both totals varying over time. Counts give a direct scale comparison, but leave unanswered how large cyclist deaths were relative to motorist deaths and do not adjust for travel exposure.

options.metric: Cyclist deaths as a percentage of motorist deaths
options.denominator: Motorist deaths in the same year
options.reason: A relative measure makes year-to-year changes in the size of the cyclist toll easier to compare despite different absolute counts.
options.answer: Cyclist deaths ranged from 10.0% of motorist deaths in 2013 to 37.8% in 2019 and stood at 28.4% in 2025.
options.interpretation: This framing answers how large cyclist deaths were relative to motorist deaths each year: the ratio peaked at 37.8% in 2019, fell to 14.2% in 2021, and was 28.4% in 2025. The ratio is a defensible comparison of relative scale, but it leaves out absolute death counts and does not measure risk per trip or person.
